subject: boundary-session-socket
text:
- **Vector:** local IPC — the driver session's socket
  - **Entry point:** `escher_driver::serve` binds one Unix-domain socket, `session.sock`, in a state directory its caller names; the hosts are the `escher-session` binary of seven_guis in its host role (`serve <task> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, its `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording; the two-argument form is gone) — run by hand or spawned by the binary's own `start` command, which re-runs the running binary (`std::env::current_exe()`) with stdin, stdout and stderr closed — and the session checks' own child processes; `serve` takes the host's idle expiry as its third parameter; the same binary's command line is the client that sends calls; no TCP or UDP port; unix only (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:36; examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:34-56)
  - **Trust boundary:** the owning user — the directory is created `0700`, a present one open to its group or to others is refused, and the socket file is set `0600`; there is no other authentication. The wire carries the lifecycle (`hello`, `stop`) and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, calls and their answers: a call brings an element id and typed text in, an answer takes ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), the snapshot's text and the diff out — the text and the diff holding, since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states, three state readings per control (selected, pressed, invalid) as closed words and booleans, inside the ratified crossing on the founder's ruling (2026-10-10, relayed by the overseer; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-snapshot-states/report.md) —, and no `NodeId` crosses — until then it was the lifecycle only and carried none of them; what is validated on it is listed under Input Validation. A boundary widening, the founder's choice (the founder, 2026-10-07, relayed verbatim), widened a second time to calls and answers and ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label «Сокет несёт команды», the English wording is the overseer's; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md) — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/report.md. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot an answer also takes the screen's pixels out: a `screenshot`'s PNG, as base64 inside its JSON line, the whole screen or one element's visible part, a password input in it painted masked (the Input Validation password row) — the in-band image the founder chose (2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer), the answer bound unchanged (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/report.md);
 an answer also takes a `lint`'s findings out — stable ids, closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour or value — the visual lint's crossing onto every ratified carrier (the Input Validation verb-table row)

subject: boundary-mcp-stdio
text:
- **Vector:** local stdio — the driver's MCP server
  - **Entry point:** `escher_driver::serve_mcp`, run by `escher-session mcp` as a stdio child an MCP client spawns under the invoking user, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface: it reads JSON-RPC 2.0 from stdin and writes its replies to stdout — no listener, port or socket — and holds the session it boots in its own process (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:44-112)
  - **Trust boundary:** the spawning client process — whatever holds the child's stdin and stdout; no authentication (the Authentication table's stdio row); validation in the Input Validation MCP server row. A result carries ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot text and an acting call's diff to the client — a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording is the overseer's) — and in the one live trial (`claude` 2.1.296 on the dev host, the operator's own login) that screen content reached the model provider through the client: what a client does with a result is the client's — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-mcp-surface/report.md. Since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the cold-agent pipe's one live run is a second carriage: through the `claude` client and the operator's own login it carried the stand's screen — element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, over 43 tool calls, no `screenshot` called — to the model provider, and the model's reply returns as the agent-written check the pipe parses and replays (the Input Validation cold-agent check row) — a boundary widening on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» (the founder, 2026-10-15, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording is the overseer's; confirmed at that chunk's wrap card, «Подтвердить (Рекомендую)») and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-15-cold-agent-test/report.md.
 Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a result also carries the screen as an MCP `image` block (a PNG, base64), a password input in it painted masked — the in-band image the founder chose (2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer); what a client does with it, a model provider included, is the client's (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/report.md);
 a `lint` result carries its findings to the client — stable ids, closed defect words and numbers — the visual lint's crossing onto every ratified carrier (the Input Validation verb-table row)

- **Boundary:** Cold-agent check (cold-agent.sh, the agent-written check)
  - **What to validate:** The model's reply, back from the live session: its last fenced ```json block, a list of tool calls the pipe replays (since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test, which deleted `scripts/cold_agent_stub.py`; the agent's tool calls themselves reach the driver's own MCP server — the MCP server row) — a new input class, a boundary widening on the founder's «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (the founder, 2026-10-15, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording is the overseer's; confirmed at that chunk's wrap card, «Подтвердить (Рекомендую)»)
  - **How (stack-specific):** `extract_check` takes only the reply's last fenced json block, at most 65,536 bytes (`MAX_CHECK_BYTES`), parsed by python `json` and required to be a JSON array; `judge_check` refuses more than 400 steps (`MAX_CHECK_STEPS`) and any step `valid_step` rejects (closed keys; `tool` one of the twelve verbs; `arguments` an object; `expect` a list of strings); a check outside these reads `no-check` or `check-failed` and is never replayed; a valid check is replayed in full, then ablated (acting steps left out), on two fresh `escher-session mcp` children spawned directly with stderr to `/dev/null` — every step validated again by the server (`validate`), every reply under a 30 s bound (`REPLY_BOUND`), each child killed and reaped, a failed child reading `check_passed` false; `check.json` is written as parsed and never printed (scripts/cold-agent.sh:274-283; scripts/cold-agent.sh:286-294; scripts/cold-agent.sh:297-336; scripts/cold-agent.sh:371-395; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-15-cold-agent-test/report.md)

- **Boundary:** Driver session socket (escher-driver)
  - **What to validate:** Request line from a local peer
  - **How (stack-specific):** One request line and one reply line per connection, `\n`-terminated, parsed against a closed grammar at wire version `v3` (`v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording): `hello v3`, `stop v3` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` — kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly (uppercase hex only, no escape of a byte that needs none, the decoded bytes UTF-8, a number in its one spelling); a known word with another version is answered `refused version`, anything else — a call the decoder does not read and a request line over 16,384 bytes included (was 64) — `refused malformed`, and runs nothing; a decoded call is run through `Session::run`, which validates it first (the Driver command schema row), and nothing else, and answered `ok v3 accepted <json>` or `ok v3 refused <json>`; a refusal or a broken connection changes nothing, a connection that ends before a line terminator gets no reply, and a `stop` takes effect once its reply is written; one connection at a time, each read and write under a 2 s bound, a client's read of a call's answer under 30 s, pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by the unix-only `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout` — the bound equal to `wire::ANSWER_BOUND`, 30 s, and a read past it on a listener that never answers `SessionError::Timeout` (packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:263-308); a lifecycle reply is bounded at 128 bytes and carries a pid, the session's label, a count and the idle expiry only; an answer is bounded at 1,048,576 bytes on its JSON line
 — over it the reply is `ok v3 oversize`, the call having run, and a call after which the host's recording ended is answered the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed` in place of its answer, the call having run and read by the client as `SessionError::RecordingFailed` — and carries what the screen reads: ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), the snapshot's text, the diff and a lint's findings, where until that chunk no reply carried any of them — the crossing ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label «Сокет несёт команды»; the English wording is the overseer's); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot an answer also carries the screen as an image — an accepted `screenshot`'s line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}`, a PNG of the whole screen or of one element's visible part, a password input in it painted masked (the password row) — the pixels in band under the unchanged 1,048,576-byte bound (the largest whole-screen answer on the stand 22,404 bytes, 2.1 % of it), ratified by the founder (2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer); since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states those two carriers also hold three state readings for an element that states one — the snapshot's text up to five more bare words of a closed set (`selected` / `unselected`, `pressed` / `unpressed`, `invalid`), a diff node up to three more keys (`selected` and `pressed` written only where present, `invalid` always written, each a boolean; twelve node keys in the schema's order, thirteen since 2026-10-12-self-description added `differs` after `bounds` on a changed node only — a list of closed words, the node-key names read from `NODE_FIELDS` by index, an added node written without it
 — a closed value set inside the ratified carrier under the same rule, each `NODE_FIELDS` row now `{ name, help }`) — never an attribute's value as typed, with no carrier, verb, argument kind, refusal cause, log field, socket or port added, the wire staying `v2` and the request grammar and its bounds as they were: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing and not a further widening, on the founder's ruling (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer: inside the ratified crossing), which also sets the rule from that day on — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening and does not come to him, while a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still does (packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:39-118; packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:156-162; packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:115-134 — the states as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-snapshot-states/report.md, `differs` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-self-description/report.md); no `NodeId` crosses; unix only, `Unsupported` elsewhere (packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:15-35; packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:179-211; packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:137-214) — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/report.md, the call, its answers and the bounds at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md (51 malformed rows in the wire's unit tests; five raw lines outside the grammar and one wrong-version line through a live socket, each refused with nothing run; the answer bound held at its edge and one byte over)

- **Boundary:** Driver session state directory (escher-driver)
  - **What to validate:** Caller-named directory path and its mode
  - **How (stack-specific):** Created mode `0700` when absent (its parent must exist); a present one whose mode grants its group or others any bit is refused (`StateDirNotPrivate`); the socket file is set `0600`; a path `std` refuses as too long for a socket address is `StateDirTooLong`, whose fixed message since 2026-10-12-self-description states the bound as a figure and holds no path — at most 94 bytes as given on Linux (measured: 94 bytes holds a session, 95 ends `state-dir-too-long`, status 3) and 90 on every other target (measured since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep on the macOS matrix leg, `aarch64-apple-darwin`: 90 bytes holds a session, 91 ends `state-dir-too-long`, status 3, with no path in the message — CI#38642493451, job 116123587286; examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:719-723) — and whose remedy is to name a shorter path or a relative one (packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:61-69); a socket file no process answers on is removed and replaced, one a process answers on is `AlreadyRunning`; `stop` — and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, the host's idle expiry — removes the socket file and then the directory, non-recursively, and nothing else is ever deleted; the path is a parameter, never an env read or a cwd-relative default (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:60-134)

  - **What to validate:** Launcher-named directory path (`--record <dir>`, `Session::recording_into`) and its mode
  - **How (stack-specific):** Since 2026-10-19-session-recording: created mode `0700` when absent (its parent must exist); a present one open to its group or to others is refused `RecordDirNotPrivate` (`record-dir-not-private`, status 3) with nothing written — and, on `start`, nothing spawned; `check-{n}.json` is created `0600` with `create_new`, `n` the smallest from 1 naming no file, so no file is ever replaced, and rewritten whole after every call through `.check-{n}.json.tmp` (`0600`) and a rename; a call no record can spell (a verb outside the eight instance verbs, a `lint` step kept like every other with its answer whole, an argument its schema does not name or passes twice) is not recorded; a failed write or a passed bound (400 records, 1,048,576 bytes) ends the recording — its check removed, nothing further recorded, `recording_failed()` true once, the call run and not rolled back, answered `recording-failed`; a file the recorder did not create is never removed; unix only (`Unsupported` elsewhere); no tool call, verb, argument or result field names the directory, and nothing of it is logged — ratified by the founder (2026-10-19, F1 A) (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:166-190; packages/escher-driver/src/recording.rs:212-257)

  - **What to validate:** A kept check's bytes, untrusted

 — every text of the answer a fixed string of the schema's tables, and `help --verb click` writing back nothing it named (packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:178-183); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `screenshot` with an optional `--id` answers one line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` on stdout, status 0 — the image by the ratified in-band crossing (the founder, 2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», relayed verbatim by the overseer) — and `--id` on an id the screen does not read exits 1 writing nothing the caller typed (examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:374-417); a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb` (the former two-argument form `<task> <state-dir>` reads so); the call the remaining words spell — an instance-level verb's arguments as flags spelt as the schema spells them, `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each followed by one value, whatever that word is, `--shift` bare, and `start`'s app as one plain word — is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for (the Driver command schema row); then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage; an argument that is not text is a usage error, and no path on argv panics; the state directory then passes `serve`'s checks above; four endings — accepted, the answer as one line of JSON on stdout, status 0; refused, the refusal on stdout, status 1; usage, one fixed line on stderr built from the verb table and the app names (`help` listed after `stop` since 2026-10-12-self-description, `screenshot` after `scroll` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot), stdout empty, status 2, nothing booted and no state created; session error, the error object on stdout — carrying the error's fixed `remedy` beside `kind` and `message` since 2026-10-12-self-description
 — and its fixed message on stderr, status 3 (the host role's was 1); the four statuses read from `EXIT_STATUSES` since that chunk — and the host role's quiet end, nothing written, status 0, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `mcp` role's end, nothing on stdout, status 0 on `Ok` and status 3 with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err`, the usage line naming the role (`; mcp role: mcp [--record <dir>]`, beside `start <app> [--record <dir>]` and `host role: serve <app> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`); no command's ending writes back anything the caller typed — no path, label, id or value — and an answer on stdout holds ids, names, values and, since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states, the three state readings (closed words in the snapshot's text, booleans in a diff node) and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's base64 PNG and a lint's findings by the ratified crossing (the Driver session socket row); a write to a closed pipe is dropped, not a panic — pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by `cli_commands`' `a_closed_stdout_drops_the_answer_and_keeps_the_ending`: with its stdout's read end closed before the run, `help` exits 0 and `snapshot --session {dir}` with no session exits 3 with exactly `SessionError::NoSession`'s fixed message on stderr, neither printing a panic, and no state directory is created (examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:649-711); `start` spawns the running binary again (`std::env::current_exe()`) as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, passing on a given `--record <dir>`, with its three streams closed, waits up to 30 s for the host to answer and neither kills nor reaps it; the command line installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable — a new external input surface, ratified by the founder with the crossing (2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option labels «Бинарник приложения, путь» · «Именованные флаги» · «Четыре класса»;

- **Boundary:** MCP server (escher-driver `serve_mcp`, the `escher-session mcp` role)
  - **What to validate:** JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and tool arguments from the MCP client that spawned the process, over that process's stdin

Returns: ` and each result field as `{name} ({kind}): {help}` — fixed table text, the listing 2,984 → 8,844 bytes; a `help` tool call answered by the server, held session or not, its text block `describe()`'s line, ending accepted, its `tool_call` span `tool` = `help` with no `command` child, counted in a held session's `served` (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp/listing.rs:50-59)
 — the program's own fixed `'static` text inside the ratified carrier, ratified by the founder (2026-10-12, «Внутри, с правилом», relayed verbatim by the overseer); and a request with no `id` a notification: no reply, nothing runs; a `tools/call`'s `params` an object with a string `name` and an optional object `arguments`, else `-32602 invalid params`, a name outside `VERBS` `-32602 unknown tool`, each argument value a string → text, an i64 → number, a bool → flag, any other refused `malformed` before anything runs, then `validate` or `validate_session` (the Driver command schema row); `start` on an app outside the binary's apps refused `malformed`; arguments arrive in key order, so a repeated key collapses to its last value and `Repeated` cannot arise over MCP; a result's text over 1,048,576 bytes (`wire::MAX_ANSWER_BYTES`) replaced by `AnswerTooLarge`'s result — since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a result that holds an image bounded by its whole written form instead, a text-only result by its text as before (`ToolResult::bounded`); the idle expiry checked when a request arrives, no timer or thread; replies written by the crate's hand-written JSON writer only, `serde_json` reading and writing nothing — no print, `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside the tests (a probe over the module, count 0); results carry ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask) and the snapshot text and a lint's findings by the crossing and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, the screen as an image

text:
- **Control:** Settle and loads in flight
  - **Configuration:** A harness settle (`Harness::settle`) reports a load in flight at once — `NotSettled` naming the class `Loads` — and never waits on one: it waits on no clock and moves none — its `animating` reading reads the overlay scrollbar fade off the document's clock — so the absent request timeout above cannot hang it, and its pass loop is bounded at 64 passes; the driver's acting step over it (`Session::act` and the executor's settled step, so `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` on every carrier) settles again every 10 ms while the answer is `Loads`, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, 5 s of wall time under the 30 s answer read below, moving no time on the held instance, then returns the load still in flight as `settled: false` with its busy class — so the absent timeout cannot hang a command either, `LOAD_WAIT` ending every wait (since 2026-10-20-load-wait); the outcome is a returned value naming a class only — no URL, request, node, id, name or value — and the counter it reads stores counts only (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:15-28; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:60-127; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:151-186; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/report.md); the driver's command schema keeps this: none of its eight instance-level verbs has an argument or a result field of a wait — the seventh, `screenshot`, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, taking one optional `id` and answering `width`, `height` and `png`, a shot resolving at the harness's own time with no tick and no pump, so it moves no time, and the eighth, `lint`, taking no argument and answering `findings`, running no step and settling nothing, so it moves none either; the overlay scrollbar fade reads the document's clock
 — on a harness-built document the harness's `VirtualClock`, which only `tick`, `advance_time` and the driver's `advance` move — so two shots of one state read the same pixels until an `advance` moves the fade, a document built with no clock still fading by wall time (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:37-103) — nor do the three session-level verbs, whose one argument is `app` and whose result fields are `label`, `pid`, `served`, `idle_expiry_s` and `stopped`, nor, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help`, which takes no argument and whose seven result fields are fixed tables — and its validation reads no clock; the command line's own bounds, 30 s for a started host to answer and 30 s on each read of a call's answer, bound a transport and wait on no load; a step that ran and did not go quiet is a result (`settled: false` with its busy class) and not a refusal, and time on a held instance moves only when a caller asks for it with `advance`, 1 to 60000 ms a call — an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, the bound the `settled` field's help states, and `snapshot`, `screenshot` and `lint` wait on none — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema/report.md
